The bytes TCKDB serves for a stored artifact are the bytes it stored, and a record whose evidence is known not to be is labelled as such at read time rather than graded as if it were intact.

If your chemistry is legitimate: Restore the object. There is no legitimate deposit this refuses — it refuses nothing — but a label that could never be cleared would be a trap, so the door is a later observation rather than an edit: the corrupt object is never deleted or overwritten by TCKDB, and re-uploading the original bytes under the same digest lets the verification pass record a ``verified`` observation that supersedes the break. A check constraint requires that row to carry a digest matching the key, so the hard fail is cleared by bytes that actually hash correctly and never by an operator asserting that they do. The break row stays as the account of what happened.

<a id="k-app-services-calculation-geometry-composition-assert-calculation-geometry-composition"></a>

### `assert_calculation_geometry_composition`

`app.services.calculation_geometry_composition:assert_calculation_geometry_composition`. block; codes [`calculation_geometry_composition_mismatch`](#c-calculation-geometry-composition-mismatch). Applied on: [`ComputedReactionUploadRequest`](#s-computedreactionuploadrequest), [`ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest`](#s-computedspeciesuploadrequest), [`ConformerUploadRequest`](#s-conformeruploadrequest), [`NetworkPDepUploadRequest`](#s-networkpdepuploadrequest), [`StatmechUploadRequest`](#s-statmechuploadrequest), [`ThermoUploadRequest`](#s-thermouploadrequest), [`TransitionStateUploadRequest`](#s-transitionstateuploadrequest), [`TransportUploadRequest`](#s-transportuploadrequest), [`ContributionBundleV0`](#s-contributionbundlev0), [`ArtifactsUploadRequest`](#s-artifactsuploadrequest).

Every geometry linked to a calculation is made of the atoms of the subject that calculation is filed under -- the species entry's own formula, or, for a transition state, the sum of its reaction's reactants.

If your chemistry is legitimate: Declare the structure's real composition: give the calculation the geometry it was run on, or file it under the subject that geometry belongs to. Absence does not block -- a ``pseudo`` owner, a transition state whose reaction records no reactants or a pseudo reactant, and an unparseable stored SMILES are all left unjudged. Only atom counts are compared, so isotopologues, scan and IRC points, constitutional isomers and dissociated optimisations all pass.

<a id="k-app-services-charge-multiplicity-reconciliation-reconcile-charge-multiplicity"></a>

### `reconcile_charge_multiplicity`

`app.services.charge_multiplicity_reconciliation:reconcile_charge_multiplicity`. warn; codes [`charge_mismatch`](#c-charge-mismatch), [`multiplicity_mismatch`](#c-multiplicity-mismatch). Applied on: [`ComputedReactionUploadRequest`](#s-computedreactionuploadrequest), [`ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest`](#s-computedspeciesuploadrequest), [`ArtifactsUploadRequest`](#s-artifactsuploadrequest).

The charge and spin multiplicity a depositor declares match the ones the electronic-structure log says the calculation was actually run at.

If your chemistry is legitimate: Absence is not contradiction: if the producing program is not one of the wired parsers, the artifact is missing, the log is truncated, or the declarations inside a single log disagree with each other, the value is left unknown and **no** warning is emitted. Only a value genuinely read from the log may contradict a declaration — emitting a mismatch because parsing failed would fabricate a contradiction out of ignorance.

<a id="k-app-services-frequency-geometry-linearity-evaluate-frequency-list-linearity"></a>

### `evaluate_frequency_list_linearity`

`app.services.frequency_geometry_linearity:evaluate_frequency_list_linearity`. warn; codes [`freq_list_linear_mode_count_for_bent_geometry`](#c-freq-list-linear-mode-count-for-bent-geometry), [`freq_list_bent_mode_count_for_linear_geometry`](#c-freq-list-bent-mode-count-for-linear-geometry). Applied on: [`ComputedReactionUploadRequest`](#s-computedreactionuploadrequest), [`ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest`](#s-computedspeciesuploadrequest), [`ConformerUploadRequest`](#s-conformeruploadrequest), [`NetworkPDepUploadRequest`](#s-networkpdepuploadrequest), [`StatmechUploadRequest`](#s-statmechuploadrequest), [`ThermoUploadRequest`](#s-thermouploadrequest), [`TransitionStateUploadRequest`](#s-transitionstateuploadrequest), [`TransportUploadRequest`](#s-transportuploadrequest), [`ContributionBundleV0`](#s-contributionbundlev0).

A frequency list's mode count should match the shape of the geometry it is attached to: ``3N - 5`` vibrations for a collinear molecule and ``3N - 6`` for a non-linear one, so a list carrying one count on a geometry of the other shape is one mode wrong in whichever direction it leans.

If your chemistry is legitimate: None needed — the warning is the accommodation, and the record is stored either way. A depositor whose molecule is genuinely quasi-linear will usually not see the warning at all, because the band between the two thresholds is deliberately silent.

<a id="k-app-services-geometry-validation-validate-calculation-geometry"></a>

### `validate_calculation_geometry`

`app.services.geometry_validation:validate_calculation_geometry`. warn; codes none. Applied on: [`ComputedReactionUploadRequest`](#s-computedreactionuploadrequest), [`ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest`](#s-computedspeciesuploadrequest).

An optimisation's output geometry still describes the species it was declared for — the optimiser handed back the molecule it was given.

If your chemistry is legitimate: The whole check is advisory, so there is nothing to escape. What a consumer must not do is read a ``fail`` row as 'this calculation is scientifically invalid'; it means only that the automated identity validator found a mismatch.

<a id="k-app-services-reaction-atom-map-warn-absent"></a>

### `_warn_absent`

`app.services.reaction_atom_map:_warn_absent`. warn; codes [`reaction_atom_map_absent`](#c-reaction-atom-map-absent). Applied on: [`ComputedReactionUploadRequest`](#s-computedreactionuploadrequest), [`NetworkPDepUploadRequest`](#s-networkpdepuploadrequest), [`TransitionStateUploadRequest`](#s-transitionstateuploadrequest).

A reaction that has a transition state should say which atom of the reactants is which atom of the saddle point and of the products.

If your chemistry is legitimate: None is needed — the warning *is* the accommodation. TCKDB deliberately will not infer a map: several chemically distinct maps are usually consistent with the same reactants and products, so choosing one by algorithm would manufacture provenance.

<a id="k-app-services-reaction-atom-map-warn-incomplete"></a>

### `_warn_incomplete`

`app.services.reaction_atom_map:_warn_incomplete`. warn; codes [`reaction_atom_map_participants_incomplete`](#c-reaction-atom-map-participants-incomplete), [`reaction_atom_map_atoms_incomplete`](#c-reaction-atom-map-atoms-incomplete). Applied on: [`ComputedReactionUploadRequest`](#s-computedreactionuploadrequest), [`NetworkPDepUploadRequest`](#s-networkpdepuploadrequest), [`TransitionStateUploadRequest`](#s-transitionstateuploadrequest).

A supplied atom map should cover every declared participant molecule, every atom of each mapped participant, and every atom of the saddle point.

<a id="k-app-services-reaction-atom-map-validate-atom-map-agrees-with-irc-evidence"></a>

### `validate_atom_map_agrees_with_irc_evidence`

`app.services.reaction_atom_map:validate_atom_map_agrees_with_irc_evidence`. block; codes [`atom_map_contradicts_irc_mapping`](#c-atom-map-contradicts-irc-mapping). Applied on: [`ComputedReactionUploadRequest`](#s-computedreactionuploadrequest), [`NetworkPDepUploadRequest`](#s-networkpdepuploadrequest), [`TransitionStateUploadRequest`](#s-transitionstateuploadrequest).

Where a deposit carries both an atom map and an IRC participant mapping for the same saddle point, they agree about which saddle-point atoms each participant is made of.

If your chemistry is legitimate: Omit one surface, or correct whichever is wrong — the mappings are optional on every path and a partial atom map is always accepted. Three absences are deliberately *not* disagreements: an atom map that omits a participant or leaves atoms unmapped is compared only over what it does claim, a transition state with no passing IRC mapping is not compared at all, and a barrierless channel has neither surface. Two participants on one side that are the same species entry are interchangeable, so a disagreement a permutation within that group would resolve is treated as arbitrary labelling rather than contradiction. A participant with no atoms is not an absence: both surfaces can say it has none -- an empty atom list -- so a reaction releasing a free electron carries a complete partition on both and is compared like any other, with the electron contributing no atoms to either side of the comparison.

<a id="k-app-services-reaction-resolution-validate-reaction-charge-conservation"></a>

### `validate_reaction_charge_conservation`

`app.services.reaction_resolution:validate_reaction_charge_conservation`. block; codes [`reaction_charge_not_conserved`](#c-reaction-charge-not-conserved). Applied on: [`ComputedReactionUploadRequest`](#s-computedreactionuploadrequest), [`KineticsUploadRequest`](#s-kineticsuploadrequest), [`NetworkUploadRequest`](#s-networkuploadrequest), [`NetworkPDepUploadRequest`](#s-networkpdepuploadrequest), [`ReactionUploadRequest`](#s-reactionuploadrequest), [`TransitionStateUploadRequest`](#s-transitionstateuploadrequest), [`ContributionBundleV0`](#s-contributionbundlev0).

The summed formal charge of a reaction's reactants equals that of its products.

If your chemistry is legitimate: Declare the free electron as a participant — ``{"molecule_kind": "electron", "smiles": "[e-]", "charge": -1, "multiplicity": 2}`` — which is how associative and dissociative attachment, photoionization and photodetachment are deposited. It contributes -1 to the side it sits on and zero atoms, so elemental balance still has to be satisfied separately. A ``pseudo`` participant suspends the law entirely, as it does for elemental balance. Conservation is not neutrality: any net charge is accepted as long as both sides carry the same one, so ion-molecule reactions are unaffected.

<a id="k-app-services-reaction-resolution-validate-reaction-elemental-balance"></a>

### `validate_reaction_elemental_balance`

`app.services.reaction_resolution:validate_reaction_elemental_balance`. block; codes [`reaction_mass_balance_failed`](#c-reaction-mass-balance-failed). Applied on: [`ComputedReactionUploadRequest`](#s-computedreactionuploadrequest), [`KineticsUploadRequest`](#s-kineticsuploadrequest), [`NetworkUploadRequest`](#s-networkuploadrequest), [`NetworkPDepUploadRequest`](#s-networkpdepuploadrequest), [`ReactionUploadRequest`](#s-reactionuploadrequest), [`TransitionStateUploadRequest`](#s-transitionstateuploadrequest), [`ContributionBundleV0`](#s-contributionbundlev0).

The reactant and product sides of a reaction contain the same number of atoms of every element.

If your chemistry is legitimate: Declare a participant with ``molecule_kind: pseudo``. A lumped or phenomenological construct has no atom-resolved composition, so one such participant suspends the law for the whole reaction. A declared electron does **not** exempt it — an electron contributes zero atoms and the reaction still has to balance.

<a id="k-app-services-reaction-resolution-validate-transition-state-composition"></a>

### `validate_transition_state_composition`

`app.services.reaction_resolution:validate_transition_state_composition` enforces 2 checks. Applied on: [`ComputedReactionUploadRequest`](#s-computedreactionuploadrequest), [`NetworkPDepUploadRequest`](#s-networkpdepuploadrequest), [`TransitionStateUploadRequest`](#s-transitionstateuploadrequest).

- **block; codes [`transition_state_composition_mismatch`](#c-transition-state-composition-mismatch).** A saddle point is made of exactly the atoms of the reaction it is declared to sit in.
  If your chemistry is legitimate: Declare the extra species as participants of the reaction. A ``pseudo`` *reactant* exempts the reaction; a pseudo product does not, and that is not an oversight — see below. Absence does not block: no geometry and no parseable SMILES means nothing is compared, and an unparseable transition-state SMILES is treated as silence rather than as a contradiction, because a TS SMILES is a lossy label for a structure that is by construction not a stable molecule. The pseudo-species exemption here is narrower than ``_load_participant_species``'s, and deliberately so. That helper exempts elemental balance and charge conservation on a pseudo participant on **either** side, because both compare one side against the other and a lumped construct makes the side it sits on unknowable. This check compares the saddle point against the **reactant side only**, so only a *reactant* being pseudo can make it meaningless; a pseudo *product* leaves the reactant side fully atom-resolved and is not exempted. Aligning the two would discard a guarantee that is still well-defined, and would discard it exactly where it is worth most: a reaction with a pseudo product has already lost elemental balance and charge conservation, so this is the only atom-level statement left about its saddle point.
- **block; codes [`transition_state_charge_mismatch`](#c-transition-state-charge-mismatch).** A saddle point carries the same total charge as the reactants it sits between.
  If your chemistry is legitimate: Omit the transition state's charge, which skips the comparison. Multiplicity is deliberately **not** checked here at all: spin is not conserved the way charge and atoms are — two doublets may react over a singlet or a triplet surface, and spin-forbidden reactions are real chemistry — so a multiplicity rule would fire on correct novel results. The pseudo-species exemption here is narrower than ``_load_participant_species``'s, and deliberately so. That helper exempts elemental balance and charge conservation on a pseudo participant on **either** side, because both compare one side against the other and a lumped construct makes the side it sits on unknowable. This check compares the saddle point against the **reactant side only**, so only a *reactant* being pseudo can make it meaningless; a pseudo *product* leaves the reactant side fully atom-resolved and is not exempted. Aligning the two would discard a guarantee that is still well-defined, and would discard it exactly where it is worth most: a reaction with a pseudo product has already lost elemental balance and charge conservation, so this is the only atom-level statement left about its saddle point.

<a id="k-app-services-reaction-resolution-validate-ts-evidence-participant-composition"></a>

### `validate_ts_evidence_participant_composition`

`app.services.reaction_resolution:validate_ts_evidence_participant_composition`. block; codes [`transition_state_irc_mapping_element_mismatch`](#c-transition-state-irc-mapping-element-mismatch). Applied on: [`ComputedReactionUploadRequest`](#s-computedreactionuploadrequest), [`NetworkPDepUploadRequest`](#s-networkpdepuploadrequest), [`TransitionStateUploadRequest`](#s-transitionstateuploadrequest).

The saddle-point atoms an IRC mapping assigns to a declared participant are that participant's own atoms, element for element.

If your chemistry is legitimate: Omit the participant mappings. They are optional on every path — evidence without them still deposits and still reads back as ``irc: present`` — so a depositor who cannot resolve the partition per atom is never forced to guess at one. Declaring a participant ``molecule_kind: pseudo`` skips that participant alone rather than the whole record, because the others' compositions are still well-defined. Isotopologues are safe by construction: both sides are compared through ``resolve_element_symbol``, so a geometry written ``D`` counts as the hydrogen its SMILES spells ``[2H]``. A free electron needs no hatch either: it is written as an empty atom list, which this check compares against the empty composition ``MoleculeKind.electron`` actually has, so a reaction that releases one is held to the same standard as every other rather than having to omit its mappings.

<a id="k-app-services-species-resolution-assert-declared-kind-matches-stored"></a>

### `assert_declared_kind_matches_stored`

`app.services.species_resolution:assert_declared_kind_matches_stored`. block; codes [`species_kind_conflict`](#c-species-kind-conflict). Applied on: [`ComputedReactionUploadRequest`](#s-computedreactionuploadrequest), [`ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest`](#s-computedspeciesuploadrequest), [`ConformerUploadRequest`](#s-conformeruploadrequest), [`KineticsUploadRequest`](#s-kineticsuploadrequest), [`NetworkUploadRequest`](#s-networkuploadrequest), [`NetworkPDepUploadRequest`](#s-networkpdepuploadrequest), [`ReactionUploadRequest`](#s-reactionuploadrequest), [`StatmechUploadRequest`](#s-statmechuploadrequest), [`ThermoUploadRequest`](#s-thermouploadrequest), [`TransitionStateUploadRequest`](#s-transitionstateuploadrequest), [`TransportUploadRequest`](#s-transportuploadrequest), [`ContributionBundleV0`](#s-contributionbundlev0).

A deposit's ``molecule_kind`` agrees with the kind already stored for the species identity it resolves to — one identity is one kind of thing.

If your chemistry is legitimate: None, and deliberately so: the escape hatch would be exactly the silent inheritance the check exists to remove. A depositor who genuinely means the stored kind declares it; one who means the other kind needs a different identity, because the two claims are about the same row.

<a id="k-app-services-species-resolution-assert-geometry-composition-matches-identity"></a>

### `assert_geometry_composition_matches_identity`

`app.services.species_resolution:assert_geometry_composition_matches_identity`. block; codes [`species_geometry_composition_mismatch`](#c-species-geometry-composition-mismatch). Applied on: [`ComputedReactionUploadRequest`](#s-computedreactionuploadrequest), [`ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest`](#s-computedspeciesuploadrequest), [`ConformerUploadRequest`](#s-conformeruploadrequest), [`KineticsUploadRequest`](#s-kineticsuploadrequest), [`NetworkUploadRequest`](#s-networkuploadrequest), [`NetworkPDepUploadRequest`](#s-networkpdepuploadrequest), [`ReactionUploadRequest`](#s-reactionuploadrequest), [`StatmechUploadRequest`](#s-statmechuploadrequest), [`ThermoUploadRequest`](#s-thermouploadrequest), [`TransitionStateUploadRequest`](#s-transitionstateuploadrequest), [`TransportUploadRequest`](#s-transportuploadrequest), [`ContributionBundleV0`](#s-contributionbundlev0).

A conformer geometry deposited under a species entry is made of the atoms that entry's own SMILES declares.

If your chemistry is legitimate: Declare ``molecule_kind: pseudo``, which has no atom-resolved composition to agree with. A free electron is deliberately **not** exempt — its composition is not unknown but empty, so any geometry deposited under one is refused, which stops ``electron`` becoming a quieter way to smuggle a structure past the check. Absence does not block: no geometry, or a SMILES RDKit will not parse, is incompleteness.

<a id="k-app-services-species-resolution-assert-geometry-isotopes-match-identity"></a>

### `assert_geometry_isotopes_match_identity`

`app.services.species_resolution:assert_geometry_isotopes_match_identity`. block; codes [`species_geometry_isotope_mismatch`](#c-species-geometry-isotope-mismatch). Applied on: [`ComputedReactionUploadRequest`](#s-computedreactionuploadrequest), [`ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest`](#s-computedspeciesuploadrequest), [`ConformerUploadRequest`](#s-conformeruploadrequest), [`KineticsUploadRequest`](#s-kineticsuploadrequest), [`NetworkUploadRequest`](#s-networkuploadrequest), [`NetworkPDepUploadRequest`](#s-networkpdepuploadrequest), [`ReactionUploadRequest`](#s-reactionuploadrequest), [`StatmechUploadRequest`](#s-statmechuploadrequest), [`ThermoUploadRequest`](#s-thermouploadrequest), [`TransitionStateUploadRequest`](#s-transitionstateuploadrequest), [`TransportUploadRequest`](#s-transportuploadrequest), [`ContributionBundleV0`](#s-contributionbundlev0).

The multiset of isotopic substitutions declared in a species entry's SMILES equals the multiset carried by the geometry deposited under it.

If your chemistry is legitimate: Deposit no geometry. An explicitly declared *standard* isotope is dropped before comparison, so ``{1: 1}`` on a hydrogen cannot fork an identity away from an unlabelled deposit of the same molecule.

<a id="k-app-services-transition-state-validation-persist-transition-state-validation-evidence"></a>

### `persist_transition_state_validation_evidence`

`app.services.transition_state_validation:persist_transition_state_validation_evidence` enforces 4 checks. Applied on: [`ComputedReactionUploadRequest`](#s-computedreactionuploadrequest), [`NetworkPDepUploadRequest`](#s-networkpdepuploadrequest), [`TransitionStateUploadRequest`](#s-transitionstateuploadrequest).

- **warn; codes [`transition_state_missing_irc_evidence`](#c-transition-state-missing-irc-evidence).** A deposited saddle point should carry passing intrinsic-reaction-coordinate evidence that it connects the declared reactants and products.
  If your chemistry is legitimate: None needed — the warning is the accommodation. Note the warning fires on absence of a *passing* ``irc`` record, so an IRC that was run and failed is stored and still warns, and so does a deposit whose only evidence is an energy ordering or an imaginary mode: neither shows the saddle point connects the declared endpoints.
- **warn; codes [`transition_state_energy_ordering_mixed_levels`](#c-transition-state-energy-ordering-mixed-levels).** The energies an energy-ordering record compares should be taken at one level of theory per energy kind.
  If your chemistry is legitimate: None needed: the warning is the accommodation. Take every energy of a kind at one level, or accept the warning.
- **block; codes [`ts_energy_ordering_stated_energy_mismatch`](#c-ts-energy-ordering-stated-energy-mismatch).** A stated energy-ordering energy should be the energy TCKDB stores for its cited calculation: the single point's (or optimisation's) energy, or for an E0 the paired electronic energy plus the cited frequency's ZPE, scaled by the stated ``zpe_scale_factor``. An E0 with no stated factor is never refused.
  If your chemistry is legitimate: State the stored energy, or cite the calculation the number came from. An E0 built with a scaled ZPE states ``zpe_scale_factor``.
- **warn; codes [`transition_state_energy_ordering_not_compared`](#c-transition-state-energy-ordering-not-compared).** Every energy an energy-ordering record states should be comparable with the energy TCKDB stores for its calculation.
  If your chemistry is legitimate: None needed: the warning is the accommodation. Deposit the cited energy (and the ZPE, at the electronic energy's geometry) to compare.

<a id="k-tckdb-schemas-stationary-point-evaluate-species-entry-frequency"></a>

### `evaluate_species_entry_frequency`

`tckdb_schemas.stationary_point:evaluate_species_entry_frequency` enforces 2 checks. Applied on: [`KineticsUploadRequest`](#s-kineticsuploadrequest), [`ReactionUploadRequest`](#s-reactionuploadrequest), [`TransitionStateUploadRequest`](#s-transitionstateuploadrequest).

- **block; codes [`n_imag_contradicts_minimum`](#c-n-imag-contradicts-minimum).** A species entry declared a minimum has no imaginary vibrational modes.
  If your chemistry is legitimate: Declare ``species_entry_kind='vdw_complex'``, which records the same mode with a warning instead, or deposit the structure through a transition-state payload if the single imaginary mode is real.
- **warn; codes [`n_imag_contradicts_minimum`](#c-n-imag-contradicts-minimum), [`n_imag_higher_order_saddle`](#c-n-imag-higher-order-saddle), [`n_imag_suggests_transition_state`](#c-n-imag-suggests-transition-state).** A van der Waals complex is formally a minimum, so an imaginary mode on one is recorded and flagged rather than refused — unless the mode is too stiff to be an intermolecular one, which suggests a genuine reaction coordinate.
  If your chemistry is legitimate: This *is* the escape hatch for the blocking minimum rule. Its own cost is that a genuinely mislabelled saddle point deposited as a van der Waals complex is accepted with a warning.

<a id="k-tckdb-schemas-thermo-declarations-thermo-declaration-error"></a>

### `thermo_declaration_error`

`tckdb_schemas.thermo_declarations:thermo_declaration_error`. Marked producer rule. Applied on: [`ComputedReactionUploadRequest`](#s-computedreactionuploadrequest), [`ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest`](#s-computedspeciesuploadrequest), [`ThermoUploadRequest`](#s-thermouploadrequest), [`ContributionBundleV0`](#s-contributionbundlev0).

  A thermo record's optional target and protocol declarations must be coherent.

  A ``single_conformer`` target names exactly one conformer group, an
  ``equilibrium_ensemble`` target none; ``protocol.version`` is exactly ``1`` and
  unknown fields and values are refused. Claims, never inferred or defaulted.

## Worked payloads: user-built composite energies

A composite energy you build yourself (a CCSD(T)/CBS extrapolation, a focal-point sum) is sent as an **assembled** composite: the other calculations are ordinary single points, and the composite is a calculation of type `composite` whose `level_of_theory` carries the recipe inline as `composite_scheme` (send `method` **or** `composite_scheme`, never both) and whose `composite_result.inputs` name, by bundle-local `key` or by `calc_...` ref, the calculation that fills each slot. The server names the level of theory itself and never stores a total it computed: it recomputes `electronic_energy_hartree` from the stored energies of the inputs to **check** yours, blocking beyond `max(1e-6, 5e-7 * n)` hartree (`composite_total_mismatch`) and warning (`composite_total_unverifiable`) when an input energy or component is not stated.

What a scheme says. The total is the sum of its terms in order. A `value` or `base` term reads one input; an `extrapolation` term applies `formula` (`inverse_power` with `exponent`, `inverse_power_shifted_half` with `exponent`, `karton_martin_scf`, `exponential_three_point`) to inputs at declared `cardinal_number`s; a `difference` term is its `high` input minus its `low` input. `energy_component` says which part of the input's energy is read. A `correlation` term means the whole correlation energy, (T) included: for an input whose stored `correlation` is the CCSD part with `triples` separate (Molpro), the server reads `correlation + triples`; for one whose `correlation` already includes (T) (ORCA), `correlation` alone. It decides by which sum equals the stored energy, and warns rather than guesses when it cannot. Formula, exponent, cardinal numbers, the input levels (including `core_treatment`) and the order of the terms are the scheme's identity; the term `key`s and the literature are not. An input level is an ordinary level: a nested composite, or a named composite method such as CBS-QB3, is refused (`composite_scheme_nested`).

### (b) CCSD(T)/CBS from a TZ/QZ pair

Reference energy at QZ, correlation energy extrapolated over cardinal numbers 3 and 4 with an inverse-power law of exponent 3. The energies are the water values printed in the ORCA 6.1 manual.

```json
{
  "species_entry": {"smiles": "O", "charge": 0, "multiplicity": 1},
  "conformers": [
    {
      "key": "c0",
      "geometry": {"xyz_text": "3\nwater\nO 0.0 0.0 0.117\nH 0.0 0.757 -0.469\nH 0.0 -0.757 -0.469"},
      "primary_calculation": {
        "key": "opt0",
        "type": "opt",
        "software_release": {"name": "orca", "version": "6.0.1"},
        "level_of_theory": {"method": "wB97X-D", "basis": "def2-TZVP"},
        "opt_result": {"converged": true}
      },
      "additional_calculations": [
        {
          "key": "sp_tz",
          "type": "sp",
          "software_release": {"name": "orca", "version": "6.0.1"},
          "level_of_theory": {"method": "CCSD(T)", "basis": "cc-pVTZ"},
          "sp_result": {"electronic_energy_hartree": -76.332111268},
          "sp_energy_components": [
            {"component": "reference", "value_hartree": -76.056728252},
            {"component": "correlation", "value_hartree": -0.275383016}
          ]
        },
        {
          "key": "sp_qz",
          "type": "sp",
          "software_release": {"name": "orca", "version": "6.0.1"},
          "level_of_theory": {"method": "CCSD(T)", "basis": "cc-pVQZ"},
          "sp_result": {"electronic_energy_hartree": -76.359705614},
          "sp_energy_components": [
            {"component": "reference", "value_hartree": -76.064381269},
            {"component": "correlation", "value_hartree": -0.295324345}
          ]
        },
        {
          "key": "ccsdt_cbs",
          "type": "composite",
          "level_of_theory": {
            "composite_scheme": {
              "kind": "extrapolation",
              "terms": [
                {
                  "key": "ref",
                  "operation": "value",
                  "energy_component": "reference",
                  "inputs": [{"slot": "value", "level_of_theory": {"method": "CCSD(T)", "basis": "cc-pVQZ"}}]
                },
                {
                  "key": "corr",
                  "operation": "extrapolation",
                  "energy_component": "correlation",
                  "formula": "inverse_power",
                  "exponent": 3,
                  "inputs": [
                    {
                      "slot": "cardinal",
                      "cardinal_number": 3,
                      "level_of_theory": {"method": "CCSD(T)", "basis": "cc-pVTZ"}
                    },
                    {
                      "slot": "cardinal",
                      "cardinal_number": 4,
                      "level_of_theory": {"method": "CCSD(T)", "basis": "cc-pVQZ"}
                    }
                  ]
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          "composite_result": {
            "assembly": "assembled",
            "electronic_energy_hartree": -76.374257395,
            "inputs": [
              {"term_key": "ref", "slot": "value", "calculation_key": "sp_qz"},
              {"term_key": "corr", "slot": "cardinal", "cardinal_number": 3, "calculation_key": "sp_tz"},
              {"term_key": "corr", "slot": "cardinal", "cardinal_number": 4, "calculation_key": "sp_qz"}
            ]
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

### (c) Focal-point additive

A QZ base plus a core-valence difference (the same level, `all_electron` against `frozen_core`), a higher-order difference, a relativistic difference and a DBOC value.

## Surface `ComputedReactionUploadRequest`

Unified upload for elementary kinetics from one computational workflow.

Payload model `tckdb_schemas.workflows.computed_reaction_upload.ComputedReactionUploadRequest`; JSON Schema `tckdb_schemas/contract/schemas/ComputedReactionUploadRequest.schema.json`.

### Will be refused if

The most specific refusals traced for this surface (ranking in the [code reference](#refusal-code-reference) intro):

- [`enthalpy_declaration_absent`](#c-enthalpy-declaration-absent) (422): Enthalpy content requires enthalpy_reference_kind.
- [`enthalpy_declaration_without_content`](#c-enthalpy-declaration-without-content) (422): enthalpy_reference_kind declares a quantity this thermo record does not carry.
- [`enthalpy_quantity_not_storable_here`](#c-enthalpy-quantity-not-storable-here) (422): Thermo accepts only formation_298k enthalpies.
- [`enthalpy_reference_kind_unrecognized`](#c-enthalpy-reference-kind-unrecognized) (422): '{reference}' is not a recognized enthalpy_reference_kind -- did you mean '{canonical}'?
- [`thermo_declaration_invalid`](#c-thermo-declaration-invalid) (422): thermodynamic_target.kind {kind} is not recognised; use {' or '.join((repr(member.value) for member in ThermoTargetKind))}.
- [`atom_map_contradicts_irc_mapping`](#c-atom-map-contradicts-irc-mapping) (422): Transition state '{subject_label}' {field_path} contradicts its own IRC participant mapping: the atom map assigns saddle-point atom(s) {disputed} to {offender[0].value} {offender[1]}, which the IRC mapping assigns to {', '.join(elsewhere) or 'no participant'} ({W_ATOM_MAP_CONTRADICTS_IRC_MAPPING}).
- [`transition_state_charge_mismatch`](#c-transition-state-charge-mismatch) (422): Transition state '{subject_label}' carries charge {transition_state_charge}, but its reactants total {reactant_charge} (transition_state_charge_mismatch).
- [`transition_state_composition_mismatch`](#c-transition-state-composition-mismatch) (422): Transition state '{subject_label}' is {format_element_counts(ts_counts)}, but the reaction it sits in is {format_element_counts(reactant_totals)} (transition_state_composition_mismatch).

### Routes

| Method and path | Success | Idempotency-Key | Path parameters | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/uploads/computed-reaction` | 201 | optional | none | `app.api.routes.uploads.upload_computed_reaction` |
| `POST /api/v1/jobs/computed-reaction` | 202 | optional | none | `app.api.routes.jobs.enqueue_computed_reaction` |

### Payload fields

Unknown keys are refused.

| Field | Type | Req | Default | Unit | Values / constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `literature` | [`LiteratureUploadRequest`](#m-literatureuploadrequest) \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |
| `software_release` | [`SoftwareReleaseRef`](#m-softwarereleaseref) \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |
| `analysis_software_release` | [`SoftwareReleaseRef`](#m-softwarereleaseref) \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |
| `workflow_tool_release` | [`WorkflowToolReleaseRef`](#m-workflowtoolreleaseref) \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |
| `rights` | [`DepositRights`](#m-depositrights) \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |
| `species` | array of [`BundleSpeciesIn`](#m-bundlespeciesin) | yes |  |  | length >= 1 |  |
| `reversible` | boolean | no | `true` |  |  | Whether the reaction is reversible. Omitted means true: an elementary step is reversible by microscopic reversibility. Send false only to state the step is irreversible. |
| `reaction_family` | string \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |
| `reaction_family_source_note` | string \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |
| `reactant_keys` | array of string | yes |  |  | length >= 1 |  |
| `product_keys` | array of string | yes |  |  | length >= 1 |  |
| `transition_state` | [`BundleTransitionStateIn`](#m-bundletransitionstatein) \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |
| `kinetics` | array of [`BundleKineticsIn`](#m-bundlekineticsin) | no | `[]` |  |  |  |
| `atom_map` | [`ReactionAtomMapIn`](#m-reactionatommapin) \| null | no | `null` |  |  | Which atom of each reactant and product is which atom of the transition state. Supplied by the depositor and never derived here: TCKDB does not run a mapping algorithm, because several chemically distinct maps are usually consistent with the same reactants and products and choosing one by algorithm would manufacture provenance (ADR 0011). Optional — a reaction deposited without one succeeds and returns a 'reaction_atom_map_absent' upload warning, because an unmapped reaction is incomplete rather than false. Requires a transition state: both legs of the map run toward the saddle point. |

### Rules the payload model enforces

- **ComputedReactionUploadRequest.validate_atom_map** (model, after; can refuse via `validate_reaction_atom_map`):

  Refuse a self-contradictory atom map; accept an incomplete one.

  Runs here rather than on a nested model because the map spans the
  reaction's participant slots, every participant's geometry, and the
  transition state's geometry — the same reason
  ``validate_ts_validation_evidence`` sits at this level.

- **ComputedReactionUploadRequest.validate_ts_validation_evidence** (model, after; can refuse via `validate_ts_evidence_set`):

  Check TS evidence against the bundle's reaction and TS geometry.

  Participant/atom completeness needs the reaction's participants, their
  declared kinds and the TS atom count, none of which the nested TS model
  can see.

- **ComputedReactionUploadRequest.validate_energy_ordering_sources_belong_to_their_participant** (model, after; can refuse):

  A participant's compared energy must come from that participant.

  ``reactant:2`` is the second entry of ``reactant_keys``; the energy
  attributed to it has to be taken from that species' own calculations,
  or the ordering compares the saddle point with some other molecule.
  The persistence seam checks ownership against the stored rows as well;
  this is the refusal that can name the keys that would have worked.

- **ComputedReactionUploadRequest.validate_reaction_family** (model, after; can refuse):

  - reaction_family_source_note requires reaction_family.
  - reaction_family_source_note is required when reaction_family is not a supported canonical family.

- **ComputedReactionUploadRequest.validate_unique_keys** (model, after; can refuse):

  - Species keys must be unique.
  - Calculation keys must be globally unique.
  - Geometry keys must be globally unique.
  - Conformer keys must be unique within species '{sp.key}'.

- **ComputedReactionUploadRequest.validate_species_key_refs** (model, after; can refuse):

  - Reaction references species key '{key}' which is not defined in the species list.
  - Kinetics fit references species key '{key}' which is not defined in the species list.

- **ComputedReactionUploadRequest.validate_calculation_key_refs** (model, after; can refuse):

  Validate every local-key reference to a calculation resolves.

  Covers the three cross-reference surfaces introduced for the
  producer-controlled provenance work:

  * ``CalculationIn.depends_on[].parent_calculation_key`` — must
    name a calculation defined elsewhere in the bundle, and must
    not equal the calculation it sits on (no self-edges).
  * ``BundleKineticsIn.source_calculations[].calculation_key`` —
    must name a calculation defined in the bundle.

  Per-key uniqueness is enforced separately by
  ``validate_unique_keys``; this validator only checks that every
  reference resolves into the bundle's calc namespace.

- **ComputedReactionUploadRequest.normalize_family** (field, after on `reaction_family, reaction_family_source_note`): applies `normalize_optional_text` to `reaction_family`, `reaction_family_source_note`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.

- **`tckdb_schemas.enthalpy_reference:enthalpy_reference_error`** (reached from `POST /api/v1/uploads/computed-reaction`):

  A thermo record with enthalpy content must declare what its enthalpies mean.

  ``enthalpy_reference_kind`` accepts one value, ``formation_298k``: every
  enthalpy on the record is a standard enthalpy of formation, pinned at
  298.15 K, with the species' own increment above 298.15 K added at other
  temperatures. It is never defaulted or inferred. Any other value is
  refused; a near-miss spelling of ``formation_298k`` gets its own refusal.

  Enthalpy content, any of which requires ``enthalpy_reference_kind`` and
  without all of which a declaration is refused:

  * ``h298_kj_mol``;
  * a ``nasa`` block or ``nasa9_intervals`` (their enthalpy constants);
  * ``wilhoit.h0_kj_mol``;
  * a point ``h_kj_mol``;
  * a point ``g_kj_mol``. A tabulated Gibbs energy is H(T) - T*S(T) on the
    record's enthalpy zero, so it carries H's reference exactly as a point
    H does, even on a point with no H of its own.

  A 0 K formation scalar has its own reference and is outside this rule.
  Never derive a missing scalar from a fit or infer a declaration.

  Returns a refusal ``(code, message)``, or ``None`` for a coherent
  declaration.

- [`thermo_declaration_error`](#k-tckdb-schemas-thermo-declarations-thermo-declaration-error) (marked rule, printed once; reached from `POST /api/v1/uploads/computed-reaction`)

### Minimal valid example

Validated against `ComputedReactionUploadRequest` when this file was generated, and accepted by every route above in the test suite.

```json
{
  "species": [
    {
      "key": "h",
      "species_entry": {
        "smiles": "[H]",
        "charge": 0,
        "multiplicity": 2
      }
    },
    {
      "key": "h2",
      "species_entry": {
        "smiles": "[H][H]",
        "charge": 0,
        "multiplicity": 1
      }
    }
  ],
  "reactant_keys": [
    "h",
    "h"
  ],
  "product_keys": [
    "h2"
  ],
  "reversible": true
}
```

## Surface `ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest`

Bundle upload payload for one computed species result.

Payload model `tckdb_schemas.workflows.computed_species_upload.ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest`; JSON Schema `tckdb_schemas/contract/schemas/ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest.schema.json`.

### Will be refused if

The most specific refusals traced for this surface (ranking in the [code reference](#refusal-code-reference) intro):

- [`enthalpy_declaration_absent`](#c-enthalpy-declaration-absent) (422): Enthalpy content requires enthalpy_reference_kind.
- [`enthalpy_declaration_without_content`](#c-enthalpy-declaration-without-content) (422): enthalpy_reference_kind declares a quantity this thermo record does not carry.
- [`enthalpy_quantity_not_storable_here`](#c-enthalpy-quantity-not-storable-here) (422): Thermo accepts only formation_298k enthalpies.
- [`enthalpy_reference_kind_unrecognized`](#c-enthalpy-reference-kind-unrecognized) (422): '{reference}' is not a recognized enthalpy_reference_kind -- did you mean '{canonical}'?
- [`thermo_declaration_invalid`](#c-thermo-declaration-invalid) (422): thermodynamic_target.kind {kind} is not recognised; use {' or '.join((repr(member.value) for member in ThermoTargetKind))}.
- [`calculation_geometry_composition_mismatch`](#c-calculation-geometry-composition-mismatch) (422): Every geometry linked to a calculation is made of the atoms of the subject that calculation is filed under -- the species entry's own formula, or, for a transition state, the sum of its reaction's reactants.
- [`species_geometry_composition_mismatch`](#c-species-geometry-composition-mismatch) (422): Species geometry is {geometry_formula}, but species_entry.smiles={payload.smiles} is {identity_formula} (species_geometry_composition_mismatch).
- [`species_geometry_isotope_mismatch`](#c-species-geometry-isotope-mismatch) (422): Isotope substitution declared in species_entry.smiles does not match the uploaded geometry. smiles={_render(from_smiles)}; geometry.isotopes={_render(from_geometry)}.

### Routes

| Method and path | Success | Idempotency-Key | Path parameters | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/uploads/computed-species` | 201 | optional | none | `app.api.routes.uploads.upload_computed_species` |

`POST /api/v1/uploads/computed-species` says:

> Bundle upload: identity + conformers + per-conformer calcs +
> artifacts + optional thermo, atomic in one transaction (DR-0029).

### Rules the payload model enforces

- **ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest.validate_unique_conformer_keys** (model, after; can refuse): conformers must have unique keys.
- **ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest.validate_unique_calculation_keys_global** (model, after; can refuse):

  Calc keys are GLOBAL across the bundle.

  Thermo source links and applied-correction source links reference
  any calc from any conformer; per-conformer scoping would force
  every reference to be a (conformer_key, calculation_key) tuple.
  Producers that want disambiguation can prefix keys
  (``conf0_opt``, ``conf1_opt``).

- **ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest.validate_dependency_keys_resolve** (model, after; can refuse):

  Every ``depends_on`` edge must name a calculation this bundle declares.

  Answers with the same code and the same ``context`` keys as
  ``app.workflows.computed_species``'s seam does for the identical
  mistake, so a depositor cannot tell which layer caught them
  (ADR 0017). The prose is unchanged from before it had a code.

- **ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest.validate_n_imag_matches_species_entry_kind** (model, after; can refuse via `raise_for_blocking_findings`):

  Refuse frequency evidence that contradicts the declared kind.

  Definitional, therefore blocking (ADR 0008).

- **ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest.validate_thermo_source_keys_resolve** (model, after; can refuse):

  - thermo.source_calculations references undefined calculation_key '{sc.calculation_key}'.
  - thermo.applied_energy_corrections[{i}].source_calculation_key references undefined calculation_key '{ac.source_calculation_key}'.

- **ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest.validate_thermo_declaration_keys_resolve** (model, after; can refuse): The thermo target's conformer and the protocol's calculations must be declared in this bundle.
- **ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest.validate_statmech_source_keys_resolve** (model, after; can refuse): statmech.source_calculations references undefined calculation_key '{sc.calculation_key}'.
- **ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest.validate_transport_source_keys_resolve** (model, after; can refuse): transport.source_calculations references undefined calculation_key '{sc.calculation_key}'.
- **ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest.validate_scf_stability_source_keys_resolve** (model, after; can refuse):

  ``scf_stability.source_calculation_key`` must name a usable job.

  Every calculation in this bundle belongs to the one species entry, so
  the owner rule is vacuous here. What is checked: the key is declared,
  it is not the carrier itself, the job is on the same conformer as the
  carrier, and no chain of keys closes into a cycle.

- **ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest.validate_statmech_torsion_scan_keys_resolve** (model, after; can refuse):

  - statmech.torsions[{i}].source_scan_calculation_key '{key}' references undefined calculation_key.
  - statmech.torsions[{i}].source_scan_calculation_key '{key}' must reference a scan-type calculation.

- **ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest.validate_top_level_applied_correction_source_keys_resolve** (model, after; can refuse):

  Top-level applied corrections may reference any calc in the
  bundle's global calc-key namespace (mirrors the thermo path).

- **`tckdb_schemas.enthalpy_reference:enthalpy_reference_error`** (reached from `POST /api/v1/uploads/computed-species`):

  A thermo record with enthalpy content must declare what its enthalpies mean.

  ``enthalpy_reference_kind`` accepts one value, ``formation_298k``: every
  enthalpy on the record is a standard enthalpy of formation, pinned at
  298.15 K, with the species' own increment above 298.15 K added at other
  temperatures. It is never defaulted or inferred. Any other value is
  refused; a near-miss spelling of ``formation_298k`` gets its own refusal.

  Enthalpy content, any of which requires ``enthalpy_reference_kind`` and
  without all of which a declaration is refused:

  * ``h298_kj_mol``;
  * a ``nasa`` block or ``nasa9_intervals`` (their enthalpy constants);
  * ``wilhoit.h0_kj_mol``;
  * a point ``h_kj_mol``;
  * a point ``g_kj_mol``. A tabulated Gibbs energy is H(T) - T*S(T) on the
    record's enthalpy zero, so it carries H's reference exactly as a point
    H does, even on a point with no H of its own.

  A 0 K formation scalar has its own reference and is outside this rule.
  Never derive a missing scalar from a fit or infer a declaration.

  Returns a refusal ``(code, message)``, or ``None`` for a coherent
  declaration.

- [`thermo_declaration_error`](#k-tckdb-schemas-thermo-declarations-thermo-declaration-error) (marked rule, printed once; reached from `POST /api/v1/uploads/computed-species`)

### Will be refused if

The most specific refusals traced for this surface (ranking in the [code reference](#refusal-code-reference) intro):

- [`calculation_geometry_composition_mismatch`](#c-calculation-geometry-composition-mismatch) (422): Every geometry linked to a calculation is made of the atoms of the subject that calculation is filed under -- the species entry's own formula, or, for a transition state, the sum of its reaction's reactants.
- [`species_geometry_composition_mismatch`](#c-species-geometry-composition-mismatch) (422): Species geometry is {geometry_formula}, but species_entry.smiles={payload.smiles} is {identity_formula} (species_geometry_composition_mismatch).

- [`species_kind_conflict`](#c-species-kind-conflict) (422): This deposit declares molecule_kind={payload.molecule_kind.value}, but the species identity it resolves to (smiles={species.smiles}, charge={species.charge}, multiplicity={species.multiplicity}) is already stored as molecule_kind={species.kind.value} (species_kind_conflict).

### Rules the payload model enforces

- **ConformerUploadRequest.validate_primary_is_not_an_assembled_composite** (model, after; can refuse via `assert_assembled_not_primary`): The primary produced the geometry; an assembled composite produced nothing (ADR 0021).
- **ConformerUploadRequest.normalize_optional_text_fields** (model, after): applies `normalize_optional_text` to `note`, `label`, `conformer_key`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.
- **ConformerUploadRequest.validate_unique_calculation_keys** (model, after; can refuse): Conformer upload calculation keys must be unique within the request.
- **ConformerUploadRequest.validate_statmech_calculation_keys_resolve** (model, after; can refuse):

  Every statmech calc reference must name a calculation declared here.

  The conformer upload has no other calc-key namespace to fall back
  on, so an unrecognised key can only be a mistake. Refusing it is
  the difference between a 422 the depositor can fix and a
  provenance link that silently never existed.

  The code is ``statmech_calculation_key_undeclared`` because that is
  what ``app.services.statmech_resolution`` answers when the same
  typo survives to the write path — this route reaches that seam, and
  ADR 0017 says the depositor must not be able to tell which of the
  two caught them.

- **ConformerUploadRequest.validate_primary_calculation_not_linked_twice** (model, after; can refuse):

  One link per (calculation, role), counting the implicit one.

  ``uploaded_calculation_role`` already links the primary
  calculation. Naming that same calculation again with the same role
  in ``source_calculations`` asks for two rows with one primary key,
  which the database refuses — better said here, where the message
  can name the field, than as a 500 mid-transaction.

- **ConformerUploadRequest.validate_additional_calculation_types** (model, after; can refuse): Additional calculation type '{calc.type.value}' is not allowed. Expected one of: {', '.join((t.value for t in sorted(_ALLOWED_ADDITIONAL_TYPES, key=lambda t: t.value)))}.
- **ConformerUploadRequest.validate_n_imag_matches_species_entry_kind** (model, after; can refuse via `raise_for_blocking_findings`):

  Refuse frequency evidence that contradicts the declared kind.

  Definitional, therefore blocking (ADR 0008).

### Rules the payload model enforces

- **KineticsUploadRequest.normalize_optional_text_fields** (model, after): applies `normalize_optional_text` to `note`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.
- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_pressure_context** (model, after; can refuse): pressure_context='apparent_at_pressure' requires pressure_bar.
- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_reported_ea_pair** (model, after; can refuse): reported_ea and reported_ea_units must both be provided or both omitted.
- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_temperature_range** (model, after; can refuse): tmin_k must be less than or equal to tmax_k.
- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_multi_arrhenius** (model, after; can refuse):

  Bind ``multi_arrhenius`` to its sum-of-terms child rows (DR-0036).

  A DUPLICATE channel is a sum of at least two modified-Arrhenius
  terms; the scalar ``a`` must stay unset because the coefficient lives
  in the child entries, and the entry indices must be unique.

- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_a_uncertainty_kind** (model, after; can refuse):

  - a_uncertainty and a_uncertainty_kind must both be provided or both omitted.
  - Multiplicative a_uncertainty must be >= 1.0 (factor f, with the true value within [A/f, A*f]).

- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_third_body_is_meaningful** (model, after; can refuse):

  PLOG and Chebyshev are never third-body reactions.

  Both parameterizations already carry the full pressure dependence, so
  CHEMKIN does not admit a ``+M`` third-body designation on them.
  Accepting the flag was not merely cosmetic: it made
  :meth:`_main_line_molecularity` raise the expected A-unit order by
  one, so a PLOG entry carrying the CORRECT units for its molecularity
  was rejected while one carrying the units of the next order up was
  accepted.

  Declared ahead of the A-unit validators so the actionable message
  wins: validators run in definition order, and the inflated-order unit
  error would otherwise mask the real cause.

- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_a_units_vs_molecularity** (model, after; can refuse via `validate_a_units_for_molecularity`): applies `validate_a_units_for_molecularity`: Raise ValueError if a_units is incompatible with the reaction molecularity.
- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_arrhenius_entries_a_units** (model, after; can refuse via `_validate_a_units_named`):

  Every summed ``multi_arrhenius`` term is the SAME reaction rate, so
  each term's ``a_units`` must match the main-line molecularity (DR-0036).

- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_plog_entries_a_units** (model, after; can refuse via `_validate_a_units_named`):

  Each PLOG pressure entry's A is the reaction's rate at that pressure,
  so its ``a_units`` shares the main-line molecularity (DR-0032 Part C).

- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_falloff_low_a_units** (model, after; can refuse via `_validate_a_units_named`):

  The low-pressure-limit k0 Arrhenius is by definition one order higher
  than k∞, so ``falloff.low_a_units`` validates at ``len(reactants) + 1``
  regardless of ``is_third_body`` (DR-0032 Part B).

- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_model_scientific_content** (model, after; can refuse): A fit must carry parameters for the declared functional form.
- **KineticsUploadRequest.default_tunneling_model_from_application** (model, before): Fill the label from the evidence block at parse time (shared body).
- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_tunneling_declaration_agrees** (model, after; can refuse via `check_tunneling_declaration_agrees`): Cross-check the tunneling label against its evidence block (shared).
- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_interpretation_content** (model, after; can refuse via `check_interpretation_set`): An interpretation set, once offered, must be complete (shared).
- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_t0_applies_to_a_scalar_rate** (model, after; can refuse):

  ``t0_k`` is only for a plain (modified-)Arrhenius record.

  PLOG entries, sum-of-Arrhenius terms, Chebyshev surfaces and the
  low-pressure limit of a falloff rate carry no T0 of their own (they are
  at 1 K). Arkane and RMG give each falloff limit an independent T0, so
  accepting one value for a lindemann/troe/sri record would silently
  mis-store k0; those forms must send ``t0_k = 1``.

- **KineticsUploadRequest._normalize_tunneling** (field, before on `tunneling_model`): applies `normalize_tunneling_model` to `tunneling_model`: Coerce a producer-supplied tunneling model to a canonical token.

### Rules the payload model enforces

- **NetworkPDepUploadRequest.normalize_text** (model, after): applies `normalize_optional_text` to `name`, `description`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.
- **NetworkPDepUploadRequest.validate_unique_keys** (model, after; can refuse):

  Ensure all local keys are unique within their respective lists,
  and that calculation/geometry keys are globally unique.

- **NetworkPDepUploadRequest.validate_key_references** (model, after; can refuse): Ensure all cross-references point to defined keys.
- **NetworkPDepUploadRequest.validate_unique_channels** (model, after; can refuse): Ensure channel identities are stable while allowing parallel paths.
- **NetworkPDepUploadRequest.validate_unique_channel_kinetics** (model, after; can refuse):

  Ensure no duplicate channel_kinetics within one payload.

  Uniqueness is keyed by ``(source_state_key, sink_state_key,
  model_kind)``: one channel may legitimately carry *both* a Chebyshev
  and a PLOG parameterization of the same k(T,P) (multiple
  parameterizations of one network coexisting on the same channel — the
  model imposes no ``(channel, solve)`` uniqueness). What remains user
  error, and is rejected here, is two entries of the *same* model_kind on
  one channel (two Chebyshevs or two PLOGs), which would silently write
  two redundant ``NetworkKinetics`` rows for one (channel, solve, kind).
  Multiple rows per (channel, solve) across separate uploads remain
  legitimate under append-only semantics.

- **NetworkPDepUploadRequest.validate_mechanistic_channel_evidence** (model, after; can refuse):

  - channel '{channel.key}' microreaction_paths must be unique by reaction and TS.
  - state_energies must provide exactly one energy for every network state.
  - channel_barriers must provide exactly one barrier for every saddle-point channel path, and none for a barrierless path.
  - channel '{channel.key}' references undefined micro_reaction_key '{reaction_key}'.
  - channel '{channel.key}' references undefined transition_state_key '{ts_key}'.
  - channel '{channel.key}' TS '{ts_key}' does not belong to micro reaction '{reaction_key}'.
  - state_energies references undefined source_calculation_key.
  - energy_transfer references undefined state_key.
  - energy_transfer references undefined collider_species_key.
  - channel_barriers references undefined source_calculation_key.
  - energy_transfer must cover exactly one entry per (well state, bath-gas collider) pair, or declare a single scope='network_wide' entry if the run specified one model for the whole network. Missing: {missing}. Unexpected: {extra}.

- **NetworkPDepUploadRequest.validate_well_skipping_channels** (model, after; can refuse):

  A well-skipping declaration must be supported by the topology.

  The scientific content of ``mechanism='well_skipping'`` is a claim
  about the network: the endpoints are *not* directly connected by an
  elementary step, and the flux reaches the sink by traversing one or
  more energized wells. Both halves are checkable against the
  ``micro_reactions`` and ``states`` already in this payload, so the
  declaration is verified rather than trusted — the backend still
  manufactures no evidence, it only reads the evidence the producer
  supplied.

  Bimolecular and termolecular configurations are reservoirs in the
  master equation: flux that reaches one has separated into products.
  Only a *well* can be an energized intermediate, so intermediates on the
  path are required to be wells.

- **NetworkPDepUploadRequest.validate_no_unused_species** (model, after; can refuse): Reject if a species is defined but never referenced anywhere.
- **NetworkPDepUploadRequest.validate_states_connected** (model, after; can refuse):

  Ensure all states form one connected component via channels.

  A PDep network must be a single connected component — disconnected
  subnetworks are not supported. If channels are provided, checks
  that every state is reachable from every other state through the
  channel graph. If no channels exist, skips this check (channels
  may be inferred later by the backend).

## Surface `ReactionUploadRequest`

Workflow-facing reaction upload payload.

Payload model `app.schemas.workflows.reaction_upload.ReactionUploadRequest`; JSON Schema `tckdb_schemas/contract/schemas/ReactionUploadRequest.schema.json`.

### Will be refused if

The most specific refusals traced for this surface (ranking in the [code reference](#refusal-code-reference) intro):

- [`reaction_charge_not_conserved`](#c-reaction-charge-not-conserved) (422): Reaction reactants total charge {reactant_charge} but products total {product_charge} (reaction_charge_not_conserved).
- [`reaction_mass_balance_failed`](#c-reaction-mass-balance-failed) (422): Reaction is not element-balanced (reaction_mass_balance_failed).
- [`n_imag_contradicts_minimum`](#c-n-imag-contradicts-minimum) (422): A species entry declared a minimum has no imaginary vibrational modes.
- [`species_geometry_composition_mismatch`](#c-species-geometry-composition-mismatch) (422): Species geometry is {geometry_formula}, but species_entry.smiles={payload.smiles} is {identity_formula} (species_geometry_composition_mismatch).
- [`species_geometry_isotope_mismatch`](#c-species-geometry-isotope-mismatch) (422): Isotope substitution declared in species_entry.smiles does not match the uploaded geometry. smiles={_render(from_smiles)}; geometry.isotopes={_render(from_geometry)}.
- [`species_kind_conflict`](#c-species-kind-conflict) (422): This deposit declares molecule_kind={payload.molecule_kind.value}, but the species identity it resolves to (smiles={species.smiles}, charge={species.charge}, multiplicity={species.multiplicity}) is already stored as molecule_kind={species.kind.value} (species_kind_conflict).
- [`species_smiles_charge_mismatch`](#c-species-smiles-charge-mismatch) (422): species_entry.charge={payload.charge} does not match SMILES charge {charge}
- [`stored_species_smiles_unparseable`](#c-stored-species-smiles-unparseable) (422): Cannot parse the stored SMILES {species.smiles} of participant {species.public_ref} while validating reaction elemental balance.

## Surface `StatmechUploadRequest`

Workflow-facing standalone statmech upload payload.

Payload model `app.schemas.workflows.statmech_upload.StatmechUploadRequest`; JSON Schema `tckdb_schemas/contract/schemas/StatmechUploadRequest.schema.json`.

### Will be refused if

The most specific refusals traced for this surface (ranking in the [code reference](#refusal-code-reference) intro):

- [`calculation_geometry_composition_mismatch`](#c-calculation-geometry-composition-mismatch) (422): Every geometry linked to a calculation is made of the atoms of the subject that calculation is filed under -- the species entry's own formula, or, for a transition state, the sum of its reaction's reactants.
- [`species_geometry_composition_mismatch`](#c-species-geometry-composition-mismatch) (422): Species geometry is {geometry_formula}, but species_entry.smiles={payload.smiles} is {identity_formula} (species_geometry_composition_mismatch).
- [`species_geometry_isotope_mismatch`](#c-species-geometry-isotope-mismatch) (422): Isotope substitution declared in species_entry.smiles does not match the uploaded geometry. smiles={_render(from_smiles)}; geometry.isotopes={_render(from_geometry)}.
- [`species_kind_conflict`](#c-species-kind-conflict) (422): This deposit declares molecule_kind={payload.molecule_kind.value}, but the species identity it resolves to (smiles={species.smiles}, charge={species.charge}, multiplicity={species.multiplicity}) is already stored as molecule_kind={species.kind.value} (species_kind_conflict).
- [`species_smiles_charge_mismatch`](#c-species-smiles-charge-mismatch) (422): species_entry.charge={payload.charge} does not match SMILES charge {charge}
- [`statmech_calculation_key_undeclared`](#c-statmech-calculation-key-undeclared) (422): source_calculations references undefined calculation_key '{sc.calculation_key}'.
- [`statmech_energy_level_ambiguous`](#c-statmech-energy-level-ambiguous) (422): see the code reference
- [`statmech_energy_level_contradiction`](#c-statmech-energy-level-contradiction) (422): see the code reference

### Routes

| Method and path | Success | Idempotency-Key | Path parameters | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/uploads/statmech` | 201 | optional | none | `app.api.routes.uploads.upload_statmech` |

`POST /api/v1/uploads/statmech` says:

> Create a standalone statmech record for a resolvable species entry.
>
> The request carries the target species-entry identity, statmech
> scientific fields, provenance references, optional inline
> supporting calculations keyed by local string, and optional
> torsions. Statmech is append-only — repeated uploads against the
> same species entry create independent rows.

Unknown keys are refused.

| `scientific_origin` | `ScientificOriginKind` | no | `"computed"` |  | `computed`, `experimental`, `estimated` | Scientific origin category for this record. |
| `literature` | [`LiteratureUploadRequest`](#m-literatureuploadrequest) \| null | no | `null` |  |  | Optional literature submission payload. |
| `workflow_tool_release` | [`WorkflowToolReleaseRef`](#m-workflowtoolreleaseref) \| null | no | `null` |  |  | Optional workflow-tool provenance. |
| `software_release` | [`SoftwareReleaseRef`](#m-softwarereleaseref) \| null | no | `null` |  |  | Optional software provenance. |
| `rights` | [`DepositRights`](#m-depositrights) \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |
| `external_symmetry` | integer \| null | no | `null` |  | >= 1 | Optional external symmetry number. |
| `rotational_constant_a_cm1` | number \| null | no | `null` | cm^-1 | > 0 | Optional A rotational constant (cm⁻¹). |
| `rotational_constant_b_cm1` | number \| null | no | `null` | cm^-1 | > 0 | Optional B rotational constant (cm⁻¹). |
| `rotational_constant_c_cm1` | number \| null | no | `null` | cm^-1 | > 0 | Optional C rotational constant (cm⁻¹). |
| `point_group` | string \| null | no | `null` |  |  | Optional point-group label. |
| `is_linear` | boolean \| null | no | `null` |  |  | Optional linearity flag. |
| `rigid_rotor_kind` | `RigidRotorKind` \| null | no | `null` |  | `atom`, `linear`, `spherical_top`, `symmetric_top`, `asymmetric_top` | Optional rigid-rotor classification. |
| `statmech_treatment` | `StatmechTreatmentKind` \| null | no | `null` |  | `rrho`, `rrho_1d`, `rrho_nd`, `rrho_1d_nd`, `rrho_ad`, `rrao` | Optional treatment classification. |
| `freq_scale_factor` | [`FreqScaleFactorRef`](#m-freqscalefactorref) \| null | no | `null` |  |  | Optional frequency scale factor ref. |
| `uses_projected_frequencies` | boolean \| null | no | `null` |  |  | Optional projected-frequency flag. |
| `optical_isomers` | integer \| null | no | `null` |  | >= 1 |  |
| `note` | string \| null | no | `null` |  |  | Optional free-text note. |
| `calculations` | array of [`StatmechCalculationIn`](#m-statmechcalculationin) | no | `[]` |  |  | Inline supporting calculations declared by key. |
| `source_calculations` | array of [`StatmechSourceCalculationIn`](#m-statmechsourcecalculationin) | no | `[]` |  |  | Statmech → calculation links by key/role. |
| `torsions` | array of [`StatmechTorsionIn`](#m-statmechtorsionin) | no | `[]` |  |  | Torsion definitions (source scans addressed by key). |
| `electronic_levels` | array of [`ElectronicLevelIn`](#m-electroniclevelin) | no | `[]` |  |  |  |
| `energy_level_of_theory` | [`LevelOfTheoryRef`](#m-leveloftheoryref) \| null | no | `null` |  |  | Optional depositor-declared level of theory the record's energy is claimed to stand at. A depositor may run the optimisation and the single point at two different levels; when declared, this must agree with what is actually linked (the linked 'sp' calculation's level, or the linked 'opt's own level when no separate 'sp' is linked) — see ``app.services.calculation_levels`` for the exact rule (R4/R5). Checked once, at upload time, against the source calculations this same request links, then stored as declared and read back as ``levels.declared_energy``. The read-time ``levels.energy`` is still re-derived from the links; the two are separate answers. |

### Rules the payload model enforces

- **StatmechUploadRequest.normalize_text_fields** (model, after): applies `normalize_optional_text` to `point_group`, `note`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.
- **StatmechUploadRequest.validate_electronic_levels** (model, after; can refuse): electronic_levels level_index values must be unique.
- **StatmechUploadRequest.validate_unique_calculation_keys** (model, after; can refuse): Statmech calculations must have unique keys.
- **StatmechUploadRequest.validate_n_imag_matches_species_entry_kind** (model, after; can refuse via `raise_for_blocking_findings`):

  Refuse inline frequency evidence that contradicts the declared kind.

  Definitional, therefore blocking (ADR 0008). The inline
  calculations are scoped to this upload's species entry, so the
  declared kind and the parsed ``n_imag`` are both present here.

- **StatmechUploadRequest.validate_source_calculation_keys_exist** (model, after; can refuse):

  Every *local* citation must name a calculation this request declares.

  Chained citations (``existing_calculation_id``) carry no key and
  are skipped here on purpose: the row they name was deposited by an
  earlier request, so this payload cannot possibly declare it. They
  are not thereby unchecked — existence, owner-consistency and
  role/type compatibility are all enforced against the database in
  :func:`app.services.statmech_resolution.resolve_or_create_statmech`,
  which is the only place that can check them.

- **StatmechUploadRequest.validate_unique_source_calculation_pairs** (model, after; can refuse):

  Refuse a repeated link, whichever way the calculation is named.

  ``statmech_source_calculation`` is keyed on ``(statmech_id,
  calculation_id, role)``, so a duplicate is a primary-key violation
  surfacing as a 500. The reference is now two-valued, so the
  uniqueness tuple carries both halves — the same shape thermo's
  ``ThermoSourceCalculationIn`` uniqueness check uses.

  One duplicate this cannot see: the same calculation cited once by
  inline key and once by id. That is impossible in practice, because
  an inline calculation is minted by this request and so has no id an
  earlier request could have handed out; the database's own primary
  key remains the backstop either way.

- **StatmechUploadRequest.validate_unique_torsion_indices** (model, after; can refuse): Torsion indices must be unique within a statmech upload.
- **StatmechUploadRequest.validate_scientific_interpretation** (model, after; can refuse):

  Scope each requirement to the claim this record actually makes.

  ``statmech_treatment`` is deliberately NOT required. Real producers
  (ARC among them) deposit symmetry, rotational constants and a
  frequency scale factor without naming a treatment; an absent field is
  honest where an invented one would not be.

  Source calculations are likewise not required here. A monatomic
  species has no vibrational modes to point at, and an experimental,
  literature or imported statmech has no calculation at all — forcing
  either to fabricate one buys nothing. Their absence on a *computed*
  record is reported as a structured upload warning at the workflow
  seam, and is enforced as an error only where a rate coefficient
  actually depends on it (the kinetics interpretation seam).

  What IS enforced is the one claim that is self-contradictory when
  unsupported: a rotor-aware treatment is *defined* by the internal
  rotors it treats, so it must list them. With no torsions the correct
  treatment is plain ``rrho``.

- **StatmechUploadRequest.validate_torsion_scan_calculation_keys** (model, after; can refuse): torsions[{i}].source_scan_calculation_key '{key}' does not reference a declared calculation.

## Surface `ThermoUploadRequest`

Workflow-facing thermo upload payload.

Payload model `app.schemas.workflows.thermo_upload.ThermoUploadRequest`; JSON Schema `tckdb_schemas/contract/schemas/ThermoUploadRequest.schema.json`.

### Will be refused if

The most specific refusals traced for this surface (ranking in the [code reference](#refusal-code-reference) intro):

- [`enthalpy_declaration_absent`](#c-enthalpy-declaration-absent) (422): Enthalpy content requires enthalpy_reference_kind.
- [`enthalpy_declaration_without_content`](#c-enthalpy-declaration-without-content) (422): enthalpy_reference_kind declares a quantity this thermo record does not carry.
- [`enthalpy_quantity_not_storable_here`](#c-enthalpy-quantity-not-storable-here) (422): Thermo accepts only formation_298k enthalpies.
- [`enthalpy_reference_kind_unrecognized`](#c-enthalpy-reference-kind-unrecognized) (422): '{reference}' is not a recognized enthalpy_reference_kind -- did you mean '{canonical}'?
- [`thermo_declaration_invalid`](#c-thermo-declaration-invalid) (422): thermodynamic_target.kind {kind} is not recognised; use {' or '.join((repr(member.value) for member in ThermoTargetKind))}.
- [`calculation_geometry_composition_mismatch`](#c-calculation-geometry-composition-mismatch) (422): Every geometry linked to a calculation is made of the atoms of the subject that calculation is filed under -- the species entry's own formula, or, for a transition state, the sum of its reaction's reactants.
- [`species_geometry_composition_mismatch`](#c-species-geometry-composition-mismatch) (422): Species geometry is {geometry_formula}, but species_entry.smiles={payload.smiles} is {identity_formula} (species_geometry_composition_mismatch).
- [`species_geometry_isotope_mismatch`](#c-species-geometry-isotope-mismatch) (422): Isotope substitution declared in species_entry.smiles does not match the uploaded geometry. smiles={_render(from_smiles)}; geometry.isotopes={_render(from_geometry)}.
